title: Plant-Based Meatball Rendang Curry
subtitle: with Cucumber Pickle and Rice
description: Enjoy all the fabulous flavours of rendang curry – but without the beef. Roll our plant-based mince into meatballs and cook in a creamy, mild curry sauce. Quick-pickled cucumber adds a piquant crunch.

steps.text: Cook rice: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.

Prep ingredients: Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Thinly slice the onion. Peel the potato, then cut into 2cm chunks. Halve the cucumber lengthwise, remove the seeds, then thinly slice (see Kitchen 101). Combine 2 tsp white vinegar and 1 tsp sugar in a bowl, season with salt, then add the cucumber and toss to combine. Set aside to pickle, tossing occasionally, until needed.

Brown meatballs: Put the plant-based mince and garlic in a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Using damp hands, combine well, then shape into walnut-sized balls. Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the meatballs, turning occasionally, for 3 mins or until browned. Remove from the pan.

Simmer curry: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in the same pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, for 3 mins or until softened. Add the curry paste and cook for 1 min or until fragrant. Add the potato, coconut milk and 250ml (1 cup) boiling water and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, covered, for 15 mins or until the potato is almost tender.

Serve up: Add the meatballs and 2 tsp soy sauce to the curry. Cook, uncovered, for a further 3 mins or until warmed through and the potato is tender. Remove the pan from the heat. Drain the cucumber, discarding the pickling liquid. Divide the rice and meatball curry among bowls, top with the cucumber pickle and enjoy!
Kitchen 101: Use a teaspoon to easily scrape out the seeds. The watery seeds add excess moisture, so removing them makes your cucumber pickle all the more crispy and crunchy!
